content.content:
1	/**
2	 * POST /api/plan — the Quicksilver decision engine.
3	 *
4	 * Request body:  { objective: string }
5	 *
6	 * Flow:
7	 *   1. Plan via @quicksilver/agent → candidateActions (ProposedAction-shaped)
8	 *   2. Resolve each referenced entity/capability/policy/evidence via Sanity
9	 *   3. Convert to kernel types
10	 *   4. Run kernel.authorize() on each candidate — this is what actually
11	 *      authorizes or blocks; it is the only authoritative step
12	 *   5. Run reviewProposedAction() as an independent second opinion — ADVISORY
13	 *      ONLY, never changes the kernel's outcome (see packages/agent/src/reviewer.ts)
14	 *   6. Persist one `decision` document per authorized/rejected candidate
15	 *      (status `awaiting-approval`, or `rejected` on a kernel hard block),
16	 *      including the reviewer's notes
17	 *   7. Return plan + kernel decisions + reviewer notes, each with its `decisionDocId`
18	 *
19	 * Response shape:
20	 *   {
21	 *     decomposition: { ... },
22	 *     reasoning: string,
23	 *     decisions: [
24	 *       {
25	 *         action: ProposedAction,
26	 *         decision: AuthorizeResult | null,   // kernel output; null if actor/capability didn't resolve
27	 *         review: ReviewResult | null,        // independent reviewer's notes; advisory only, null if not resolved
28	 *         decisionDocId: string | null,       // Sanity _id of the persisted decision; null if not persisted
29	 *         resolvedReferences: {
30	 *           actor: { id, name, entityType },
31	 *           capability: { id, name, riskLevel },
32	 *           policies: [{ id, name, scope, priority }],
33	 *           evidence: [{ id, title, confidence }],
34	 *         }
35	 *       },
36	 *       ...
37	 *     ]
38	 *   }
39	 */
40	
41	import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
42	import { createClient } from '@sanity/client'
43	import { z } from 'zod'
44	import { isLlmConfigured, planObjective, reviewProposedAction, type ReviewResult } from '@quicksilver/agent'
45	import {
46	  authorize,
47	  type AuthorizeResult,
48	  type CapabilityRef,
49	  type EntityRef,
50	  type EntityType,
51	  type EvidenceRef,
52	  type PolicyRef,
53	  type ProposedAction,
54	  type RiskLevel,
55	} from '@quicksilver/kernel'
56	
57	function getSanityClient() {
58	  return createClient({
59	    projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID!,
60	    dataset: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET ?? 'production',
61	    apiVersion: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_API_VERSION ?? '2024-10-01',
62	    useCdn: false,
63	    // Server-side read + write; needs an Editor-scoped token to persist decisions.
64	    token: process.env.SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN,
65	  })
66	}
67	
68	// ── Resolution: planner IDs → kernel refs ──────────────────────────────────
69	
70	type Resolved = {
71	  actor: EntityRef | null
72	  capability: CapabilityRef | null
73	  policies: PolicyRef[]
74	  evidence: EvidenceRef[]
75	}
76	
77	async function resolveAction(
78	  client: ReturnType<typeof getSanityClient>,
79	  action: ProposedAction,
80	): Promise<Resolved> {
81	  // NOTE on the GROQ below: reference arrays are read with `arr[]._ref` (the raw
82	  // reference keys), NOT `arr[]->._ref` — dereferencing returns the target
83	  // document, which has no `_ref`, so that yields `[null]`. Each projection is
84	  // aliased to the key this function reads.
85	  const [actorDoc, capabilityDoc, policyDocs, evidenceDocs] = await Promise.all([
86	    client.fetch<{ _id: string; name: string; entityType: string; capabilityIds?: string[] | null } | null>(
87	      `*[_type == "entity" && _id == $id][0]{ _id, name, entityType, "capabilityIds": capabilities[]._ref }`,
88	      { id: action.actorId },
89	    ),
90	    client.fetch<{ _id: string; name: string; riskLevel?: number | null; authorizedEntityIds?: string[] | null } | null>(
91	      `*[_type == "capability" && _id == $id][0]{ _id, name, riskLevel, "authorizedEntityIds": authorizedEntities[]._ref }`,
92	      { id: action.capabilityId },
93	    ),
94	    client.fetch<
95	      Array<{
96	        _id: string
97	        name: string
98	        scope: string
99	        priority: number
100	        effectiveDate?: string | null
101	        expirationDate?: string | null
102	        supersedesIds?: string[] | null
103	        approvalRequirementIds?: string[] | null
104	      }>
105	    >(
106	      `*[_type == "policy" && _id in $ids]{ _id, name, scope, priority, effectiveDate, expirationDate, "supersedesIds": supersedes[]._ref, "approvalRequirementIds": approvalRequirements[]._ref }`,
107	      { ids: action.applicablePolicyIds },
108	    ),
109	    client.fetch<Array<{ _id: string; title: string; confidence: number }>>(
110	      `*[_type == "evidence" && _id in $ids]{ _id, title, confidence }`,
111	      { ids: action.evidenceIds },
112	    ),
113	  ])
114	
115	  const actor: EntityRef | null = actorDoc
116	    ? {
117	        id: actorDoc._id,
118	        name: actorDoc.name,
119	        entityType: actorDoc.entityType as EntityType,
120	        capabilityIds: actorDoc.capabilityIds ?? [],
121	      }
122	    : null
123	
124	  const capability: CapabilityRef | null = capabilityDoc
125	    ? {
126	        id: capabilityDoc._id,
127	        name: capabilityDoc.name,
128	        baseRiskLevel: (capabilityDoc.riskLevel ?? 2) as RiskLevel,
129	        authorizedEntityIds: capabilityDoc.authorizedEntityIds ?? [],
130	      }
131	    : null
132	
133	  const policies: PolicyRef[] = policyDocs.map((p) => ({
134	    id: p._id,
135	    name: p.name,
136	    scope: p.scope,
137	    priority: p.priority,
138	    effectiveDate: p.effectiveDate ?? undefined,
139	    expirationDate: p.expirationDate ?? undefined,
140	    supersedesIds: p.supersedesIds ?? [],
141	    approvalRequirementIds: p.approvalRequirementIds ?? [],
142	  }))
143	
144	  const evidence: EvidenceRef[] = evidenceDocs.map((e) => ({
145	    id: e._id,
146	    title: e.title,
147	    confidence: e.confidence,
148	  }))
149	
150	  return { actor, capability, policies, evidence }
151	}
152	
153	// ── Persistence: kernel result → `decision` document ───────────────────────
154	
155	const ref = (id: string) => ({ _type: 'reference' as const, _ref: id, _key: id })
156	
157	/**
158	 * Build the auditable decision record (schema: apps/studio/schemas/decision.ts).
159	 * Only references documents that were actually resolved from Sanity — a planner-
160	 * invented ID must never become a dangling strong reference.
161	 */
162	function buildDecisionDoc(args: {
163	  id: string
164	  objective: string
165	  constraints: string[]
166	  reasoning: string
167	  action: ProposedAction
168	  refs: Resolved & { actor: EntityRef; capability: CapabilityRef }
169	  decision: AuthorizeResult
170	  review: ReviewResult | null
171	  now: string
172	}) {
173	  const { id, objective, constraints, reasoning, action, refs, decision, review, now } = args
174	
175	  // The kernel reports conflicts per shared scope as text; mark every applicable
176	  // policy in a shared scope as `conflicts` in the per-policy audit rows.
177	  const scopeCount = new Map<string, number>()
178	  for (const c of decision.policyChecks) {
179	    if (c.result !== 'applies') continue
180	    const scope = refs.policies.find((p) => p.id === c.policyId)?.scope
181	    if (scope) scopeCount.set(scope, (scopeCount.get(scope) ?? 0) + 1)
182	  }
183	
184	  return {
185	    _id: id,
186	    _type: 'decision' as const,
187	    question: objective,
188	    context: [refs.actor.id, refs.capability.id, ...refs.policies.map((p) => p.id)].map(ref),
189	    candidateActions: [
190	      {
191	        _key: 'k0',
192	        description: action.description,
193	        actor: { _type: 'reference' as const, _ref: refs.actor.id },
194	        capability: { _type: 'reference' as const, _ref: refs.capability.id },
195	      },
196	    ],
197	    selectedAction: action.description,
198	    reasoningSummary: reasoning,
199	    evidence: refs.evidence.map((e) => e.id).map(ref),
200	    constraints,
201	    policyChecks: decision.policyChecks.map((c) => {
202	      const scope = refs.policies.find((p) => p.id === c.policyId)?.scope
203	      const conflicted = c.result === 'applies' && scope !== undefined && (scopeCount.get(scope) ?? 0) > 1
204	      return {
205	        _key: c.policyId,
206	        policy: { _type: 'reference' as const, _ref: c.policyId },
207	        result: conflicted ? 'conflicts' : c.result,
208	        reason: conflicted ? `${c.reason} Shares this scope with another applicable policy.` : c.reason,
209	      }
210	    }),
211	    riskLevel: decision.riskLevel,
212	    requiredApproval: decision.requiresApproval,
213	    reviewerNotes: review
214	      ? {
215	          valid: review.valid,
216	          policyConflicts: review.policyConflicts,
217	          missingEvidence: review.missingEvidence,
218	          riskConcerns: review.riskConcerns,
219	          suggestions: review.suggestions,
220	        }
221	      : undefined,
222	    status: decision.recommendation === 'reject' ? ('rejected' as const) : ('awaiting-approval' as const),
223	    createdAt: now,
224	  }
225	}
226	
227	// ── Request validation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
228	
229	const BodySchema = z.object({
230	  objective: z.string().min(3).max(2000),
231	})
232	
233	export async function POST(req: Request) {
234	  let body: unknown
235	  try {
236	    body = await req.json()
237	  } catch {
238	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid JSON body' }, { status: 400 })
239	  }
240	
241	  const parsed = BodySchema.safeParse(body)
242	  if (!parsed.success) {
243	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Validation failed', issues: parsed.error.issues }, { status: 400 })
244	  }
245	  const { objective } = parsed.data
246	
247	  if (!isLlmConfigured()) {
248	    return NextResponse.json(
249	      {
250	        error:
251	          'No LLM configured on the server. Set AZURE_API_KEY and AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME (or OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY) in the root .env.',
252	      },
253	      { status: 500 },
254	    )
255	  }
256	  if (!process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID) {
257	    return NextResponse.json(
258	      { error: 'Sanity project ID not configured.' },
259	      { status: 500 },
260	    )
261	  }
262	
263	  try {
264	    const client = getSanityClient()
265	    const plan = await planObjective({ objective })
266	    const now = new Date().toISOString()
267	    const runId = Date.now().toString(36)
268	
269	    // Run each candidate action through the kernel.
270	    const results = await Promise.all(
271	      plan.candidateActions.map(async (action, i) => {
272	        const refs = await resolveAction(client, action as ProposedAction)
273	        let decision: AuthorizeResult | null = null
274	        let review: ReviewResult | null = null
275	        let doc: ReturnType<typeof buildDecisionDoc> | null = null
276	
277	        if (refs.actor && refs.capability) {
278	          // Construct a kernel-compatible ProposedAction. The planner returns
279	          // Zod-inferred numeric fields, but the kernel wants the RiskLevel
280	          // union (0–5). Cast at the boundary.
281	          const kernelAction: ProposedAction = {
282	            description: action.description,
283	            actorId: action.actorId,
284	            capabilityId: action.capabilityId,
285	            applicablePolicyIds: action.applicablePolicyIds,
286	            evidenceIds: action.evidenceIds,
287	            financialExposure: action.financialExposure,
288	            reversible: action.reversible,
289	            operationalImpact: action.operationalImpact as RiskLevel,
290	            uncertainty: action.uncertainty as RiskLevel,
291	          }
292	          decision = authorize({
293	            action: kernelAction,
294	            actor: refs.actor,
295	            capabilities: [refs.capability],
296	            policies: refs.policies,
297	            evidence: refs.evidence,
298	          })
299	
300	          // Independent review — advisory only. The kernel above has already
301	          // authorized/rejected the action; the reviewer never changes that
302	          // outcome, it only adds a second opinion for the human approver to
303	          // see. A reviewer failure (bad output, provider error) must not
304	          // block the plan response, so reviewProposedAction() always
305	          // resolves (see its own fallback) rather than throwing.
306	          review = await reviewProposedAction({
307	            action: kernelAction,
308	            actor: { id: refs.actor.id, name: refs.actor.name, entityType: refs.actor.entityType },
309	            capability: {
310	              id: refs.capability.id,
311	              name: refs.capability.name,
312	              riskLevel: refs.capability.baseRiskLevel,
313	            },
314	            policies: refs.policies.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, name: p.name, scope: p.scope, priority: p.priority })),
315	            evidence: refs.evidence,
316	          })
317	
318	          doc = buildDecisionDoc({
319	            id: `decision-plan-${runId}-${i}`,
320	            objective,
321	            constraints: plan.decomposition.constraints,
322	            reasoning: plan.reasoning,
323	            action: kernelAction,
324	            refs: { ...refs, actor: refs.actor, capability: refs.capability },
325	            decision,
326	            review,
327	            now,
328	          })
329	        }
330	
331	        return { action: action as ProposedAction, decision, review, refs, doc }
332	      }),
333	    )
334	
335	    // Persist every decision atomically. Failure here is loud on purpose: without
336	    // a decision document the Approve → Execute → Observe loop cannot proceed.
337	    const docs = results.flatMap((r) => (r.doc ? [r.doc] : []))
338	    if (docs.length > 0) {
339	      const tx = client.transaction()
340	      for (const d of docs) tx.create(d)
341	      await tx.commit()
342	    }
343	
344	    const decisions = results.map((r) => ({
345	      action: r.action,
346	      decision: r.decision,
347	      review: r.review,
348	      decisionDocId: r.doc?._id ?? null,
349	      resolvedReferences: {
350	        actor: r.refs.actor && {
351	          id: r.refs.actor.id,
352	          name: r.refs.actor.name,
353	          entityType: r.refs.actor.entityType,
354	        },
355	        capability: r.refs.capability && {
356	          id: r.refs.capability.id,
357	          name: r.refs.capability.name,
358	          riskLevel: r.refs.capability.baseRiskLevel,
359	        },
360	        policies: r.refs.policies.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, name: p.name, scope: p.scope, priority: p.priority })),
361	        evidence: r.refs.evidence,
362	      },
363	    }))
364	
365	    return NextResponse.json({
366	      decomposition: plan.decomposition,
367	      reasoning: plan.reasoning,
368	      decisions,
369	    })
370	  } catch (err) {
371	    console.error('[/api/plan]', err)
372	    return NextResponse.json(
373	      { error: 'Plan failed', detail: (err as Error).message },
374	      { status: 500 },
375	    )
376	  }
377	}

1	/**
2	 * Reviewer — an independent second opinion on a proposed action.
3	 *
4	 * Wired into /api/plan (apps/web) alongside the kernel's own authorize()
5	 * call. The reviewer NEVER authorizes or blocks anything — only the kernel
6	 * does that (packages/kernel). It flags concerns for a human approver to
7	 * see alongside the kernel's risk/policy computation, and its notes are
8	 * persisted on the `decision` document (field: `reviewerNotes`) for
9	 * auditability.
10	 *
11	 * Previously REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT existed but was only exercised by the
12	 * standalone verify-llm.ts health check, never in the live request path.
13	 * This file is what actually calls it for real.
14	 */
15	
16	import { generateText, Output } from 'ai'
17	import { z } from 'zod'
18	
19	import { REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT } from './prompts.ts'
20	import { modelForRole } from './models.ts'
21	import type { ProposedAction } from '@quicksilver/kernel'
22	
23	export const ReviewResultSchema = z.object({
24	  valid: z.boolean(),
25	  policyConflicts: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
26	  missingEvidence: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
27	  riskConcerns: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
28	  suggestions: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
29	})
30	
31	export type ReviewResult = z.infer<typeof ReviewResultSchema>
32	
33	export interface ReviewInput {
34	  action: ProposedAction
35	  actor: { id: string; name: string; entityType: string }
36	  capability: { id: string; name: string; riskLevel: number }
37	  policies: Array<{ id: string; name: string; scope: string; priority: number }>
38	  evidence: Array<{ id: string; title: string; confidence: number }>
39	}
40	
41	/** A neutral, clearly-labeled fallback when the reviewer call itself fails or
42	 *  returns no structured output — the kernel is still authoritative either
43	 *  way, so a reviewer hiccup must never block the plan response. */
44	function unreviewed(reason: string): ReviewResult {
45	  return {
46	    valid: true,
47	    policyConflicts: [],
48	    missingEvidence: [],
49	    riskConcerns: [`Reviewer unavailable: ${reason}`],
50	    suggestions: [],
51	  }
52	}
53	
54	export async function reviewProposedAction(input: ReviewInput): Promise<ReviewResult> {
55	  const { action, actor, capability, policies, evidence } = input
56	
57	  const policyList = policies.length
58	    ? policies.map((p) => `- ${p.name} (scope: ${p.scope}, priority: ${p.priority}, id: ${p.id})`).join('\n')
59	    : '(none resolved)'
60	  const evidenceList = evidence.length
61	    ? evidence.map((e) => `- ${e.title} (confidence: ${e.confidence}, id: ${e.id})`).join('\n')
62	    : '(none resolved)'
63	
64	  try {
65	    const result = await generateText({
66	      model: modelForRole('reviewer'),
67	      system: REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
68	      prompt: `Proposed action: ${action.description}
69	
70	Actor: ${actor.name} (${actor.entityType}, id ${actor.id})
71	Capability: ${capability.name} (base risk ${capability.riskLevel}/5, id ${capability.id})
72	
73	Applicable policies:
74	${policyList}
75	
76	Supporting evidence:
77	${evidenceList}
78	
79	Financial exposure: $${action.financialExposure}
80	Reversible: ${action.reversible}
81	Operational impact: ${action.operationalImpact}/5
82	Uncertainty: ${action.uncertainty}/5
83	
84	Review this proposed action independently. Flag any policy conflicts, missing evidence, or risk concerns you see. Do not simply restate the kernel's own computation -- add what an independent reviewer would actually catch.`,
85	      experimental_output: Output.object({ schema: ReviewResultSchema }),
86	      maxRetries: 1,
87	    } as Parameters<typeof generateText>[0])
88	
89	    const parsed = (result as unknown as { experimental_output?: ReviewResult }).experimental_output
90	    return parsed ?? unreviewed('model did not return structured output')
91	  } catch (err) {
92	    return unreviewed((err as Error).message)
93	  }
94	}

1	/**
2	 * POST /api/plan — the Quicksilver decision engine.
3	 *
4	 * Request body:  { objective: string }
5	 *
6	 * Flow:
7	 *   1. Plan via @quicksilver/agent → candidateActions (ProposedAction-shaped)
8	 *   2. Resolve each referenced entity/capability/policy/evidence via Sanity
9	 *   3. Convert to kernel types
10	 *   4. Run kernel.authorize() on each candidate — this is what actually
11	 *      authorizes or blocks; it is the only authoritative step
12	 *   5. Run reviewProposedAction() as an independent second opinion — ADVISORY
13	 *      ONLY, never changes the kernel's outcome (see packages/agent/src/reviewer.ts)
14	 *   6. Persist one `decision` document per authorized/rejected candidate
15	 *      (status `awaiting-approval`, or `rejected` on a kernel hard block),
16	 *      including the reviewer's notes
17	 *   7. Return plan + kernel decisions + reviewer notes, each with its `decisionDocId`
18	 *
19	 * Response shape:
20	 *   {
21	 *     decomposition: { ... },
22	 *     reasoning: string,
23	 *     decisions: [
24	 *       {
25	 *         action: ProposedAction,
26	 *         decision: AuthorizeResult | null,   // kernel output; null if actor/capability didn't resolve
27	 *         review: ReviewResult | null,        // independent reviewer's notes; advisory only, null if not resolved
28	 *         decisionDocId: string | null,       // Sanity _id of the persisted decision; null if not persisted
29	 *         resolvedReferences: {
30	 *           actor: { id, name, entityType },
31	 *           capability: { id, name, riskLevel },
32	 *           policies: [{ id, name, scope, priority }],
33	 *           evidence: [{ id, title, confidence }],
34	 *         }
35	 *       },
36	 *       ...
37	 *     ]
38	 *   }
39	 */
40	
41	import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
42	import { createClient } from '@sanity/client'
43	import { z } from 'zod'
44	import { isLlmConfigured, planObjective, reviewProposedAction, type ReviewResult } from '@quicksilver/agent'
45	import {
46	  authorize,
47	  type AuthorizeResult,
48	  type CapabilityRef,
49	  type EntityRef,
50	  type EntityType,
51	  type EvidenceRef,
52	  type PolicyRef,
53	  type ProposedAction,
54	  type RiskLevel,
55	} from '@quicksilver/kernel'
56	
57	function getSanityClient() {
58	  return createClient({
59	    projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID!,
60	    dataset: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET ?? 'production',
61	    apiVersion: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_API_VERSION ?? '2024-10-01',
62	    useCdn: false,
63	    // Server-side read + write; needs an Editor-scoped token to persist decisions.
64	    token: process.env.SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN,
65	  })
66	}
67	
68	// ── Resolution: planner IDs → kernel refs ──────────────────────────────────
69	
70	type Resolved = {
71	  actor: EntityRef | null
72	  capability: CapabilityRef | null
73	  policies: PolicyRef[]
74	  evidence: EvidenceRef[]
75	}
76	
77	async function resolveAction(
78	  client: ReturnType<typeof getSanityClient>,
79	  action: ProposedAction,
80	): Promise<Resolved> {
81	  // NOTE on the GROQ below: reference arrays are read with `arr[]._ref` (the raw
82	  // reference keys), NOT `arr[]->._ref` — dereferencing returns the target
83	  // document, which has no `_ref`, so that yields `[null]`. Each projection is

162	function buildDecisionDoc(args: {
163	  id: string
164	  objective: string
165	  constraints: string[]
166	  reasoning: string
167	  action: ProposedAction

177	  const scopeCount = new Map<string, number>()

179	    if (c.result !== 'applies') continue

181	    if (scope) scopeCount.set(scope, (scopeCount.get(scope) ?? 0) + 1)

204	      return {

206	        policy: { _type: 'reference' as const, _ref: c.policyId },

263	  try {

265	    const plan = await planObjective({ objective })
266	    const now = new Date().toISOString()
267	    const runId = Date.now().toString(36)
268	
269	    // Run each candidate action through the kernel.
270	    const results = await Promise.all(
271	      plan.candidateActions.map(async (action, i) => {
272	        const refs = await resolveAction(client, action as ProposedAction)
273	        let decision: AuthorizeResult | null = null

277	        if (refs.actor && refs.capability) {
278	          // Construct a kernel-compatible ProposedAction. The planner returns
279	          // Zod-inferred numeric fields, but the kernel wants the RiskLevel
280	          // union (0–5). Cast at the boundary.
281	          const kernelAction: ProposedAction = {

# Quicksilver

> **An Autonomous Company Operating System.**
> Structured organizational knowledge → agent reasoning → deterministic authority → recorded decision → state update.

Submitted to the **Sanity Challenge (Sept 18 – Oct 4, 2026)**: Path One (*Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content*) and Path Two (*Vibe-Code Something Strange*).

---

## The thesis

A chatbot reads your documents. **Quicksilver reasons over your company.**

The difference is structural: an LLM with access to ordinary documents answers questions. An LLM with access to a structured **company model** — entities, capabilities, policies, evidence, objectives, workflows — can determine *what the company should do*, propose a course of action, route it through a deterministic authority kernel, and record the result as state.

```
CEO: "Reduce production downtime by 20%."
              ↓
       QUICKSILVER
              ↓
   Sanity Context (MCP, read-only)
              ↓
   Structured company model (GROQ + Knowledge Base)
              ↓
   Candidate plan (planner model)
              ↓
   Independent review (reviewer model)
              ↓
   Quicksilver Kernel (capability + authority + risk + approval)
              ↓
        APPROVAL GATE
        /         \
   autonomous     human
        \         /
         \       /
          state update
```

---

---PATH-ONE---
is a real Sanity document.

The kernel is plain TypeScript. No LLM inside it. The LLM proposes a
candidate action; the kernel decides whether the actor has the
capability, which policies apply, how the risk stacks up, and whether
the action is allowed to execute autonomously, requires human approval,
or is hard-blocked. Hard blocks (no capability granted, no evidence
available) reject. Soft concerns (policy conflicts, low evidence
confidence) escalate to approval. Risk above the org-defined threshold
always escalates.

Models are role-based. The planner is `gpt-5.6-sol` (or
`gemini-3.8-flash` after a bake-off — Google's positioning of 3.8 Flash
as "engineered for autonomous agents and complex enterprise workflows"
makes it a serious candidate). The reviewer is `claude-sonnet-5`, which
flags concerns independently. Neither reviewer nor planner is allowed
to authorize. The kernel is authoritative.

## What the demo proves

Drop in the seed objective: *"Reduce production downtime by 20% over the
next 30 days without increasing OPEX."* The agent decomposes it,
identifies the relevant policies (Operations Policy 17 and Emergency
Policy 4, both in scope `production.parameter_changes`), and proposes
adjusting a CNC controller parameter by 5%. The kernel's authority
check surfaces the conflict (same scope, priority 5 vs. priority 7) and
the historical-incident evidence that contradicts the parameter-adjustment
hypothesis (confidence 0.92). Risk computes to 4 of 5. Reversibility is
partial. The recommendation routes to **human approval**.

Approve, execute (simulated), observe a metric moved 32 → 25.6 hours
---PATH-TWO---
approval UI as one component, then close the loop with simulated
execution and rollback.

What I deliberately **didn't** build, and why:
- A multi-objective dashboard. One CEO-intent box, one plan, one
  decision at a time. A grid of "active objectives" is a bigger UI
  than a three-judge demo needs.
- Real production control. The demo is safe; a real CNC would not be.
- Multi-tenant architecture. Single user, one demo path.
- Auth complexity. Single-user demo, no signup.
- CRM, HR, payroll, billing. ERP is the trap. The trap costs you the
  contest.
- A "general-purpose autonomous agent marketplace." That's a
  different product.
- Many specialized agents (CEO Agent, COO Agent, CFO Agent, …).
  Sounds impressive, drowns the demo in orchestration complexity.
  One primary agent + reviewer + deterministic kernel is enough.

## Why Path Two specifically

Path Two is judged on quality of build process, finish, schema
thoughtfulness, and originality — *not* on which AI features you
wrapped. So I treated it as a single-author, scope-disciplined build:
lock the schema on Day 1, ship something runnable every day, defer the
polish to the last two days, don't add anything the judging criteria
didn't ask for.
---SUBMISSION---

The **Quicksilver Kernel** is a deterministic TypeScript library that:

- checks capability (does the actor have it AND is it granted)
- checks authority (which policies apply, which are superseded, which conflict)
- computes risk (deterministic formula clamped 0–5)
- routes to approval gate (autonomous / request-approval / reject)

The **LLM proposes, the kernel authorizes**. Never the other way around.

The **AI SDK 6 agent harness** uses `@ai-sdk/mcp` with role-based model
configuration:

- **planner**: `gpt-5.6-sol` (or `gemini-3.8-flash` after bake-off)
- **reviewer**: `claude-sonnet-5`
- **router**: `gpt-5.6-luna`
- **executor**: `gemini-3.8-flash`

All reads go through Sanity Context MCP; all writes go through
`@sanity/client` mutations against the HTTP API (Context MCP is read-only).

## What we deliberately did NOT build

- Real production control
- Multi-tenant architecture
- Auth complexity (single-user demo)
- Multiple specialized agents (one primary agent + reviewer)
- CRM, HR, payroll, billing — full ERP

That's future Quicksilver. Competition Quicksilver proves the operating-system
abstraction, end-to-end, with one vertical slice.

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/pre-submission-audit-2026-09-21.md","content":"# Quicksilver pre-submission audit (2026-09-21)

## Status: the five blockers are fixed in the repo (same day)

Verified in a scratch copy with the new dependency set: kernel tests 14/14, agent model tests 10/10, an end-to-end route flow (plan -> persist -> approve -> execute -> observe) against the real seed data (52 docs) in an in-memory Sanity, `tsc --noEmit` clean for kernel/agent/web, and `next build` succeeds. The new threshold tests fail against the old `approval.ts`, as they should.

NOT verified (needs live credentials): Azure deployments (strict JSON-schema output, Responses API on your chosen models), the live Sanity Context MCP, and `npm run setup:azure` against the real Azure CLI (tested against a fake `az`, on Linux only).

### What changed
- **Kernel** (`approval.ts`): risk thresholds read via `readRiskThreshold()` with explicit defaults (auto max 2, review 3); unset/empty/garbage/out-of-range env falls back instead of NaN. `AuthorizeResult` now carries `policyChecks`. `types.ts` accepts `null` for `expirationDate`/`reportsToId` (what Sanity returns). 5 new tests.
- **/api/plan**: GROQ fixed (`arr[]._ref`, aliased); persists one `decision` doc per candidate in a single transaction (`decision-plan-<run>-<i>`, status `awaiting-approval`, or `rejected` on a kernel hard block) and returns `decisionDocId`; response now matches its documented shape (`capability.riskLevel`); uses `isLlmConfigured()` instead of requiring `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **/observe**: `"evidenceIds": evidence[]._ref`.
- **/action** (beyond the five): only `awaiting-approval`/`proposed` decisions can be acted on (409 otherwise, so a kernel `reject` is final); approval no longer stamps `executedAt`.
- **AI SDK**: whole stack aligned on the v6 line (`ai@6`, `@ai-sdk/azure@3`, `openai@3`, `anthropic@3`, `google@3`, `openai-compatible@2` for Ollama, `mcp@1`). The old mix was `ai@5` + `anthropic@1` + `azure@4` (spec v4), which cannot work together. Azure is the default provider when `AZURE_API_KEY` + `AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME` are set; deployments `qs-planner|reviewer|router|executor`. Lockfile regenerated.
- **Found while fixing** (not in the original list): `generateText` defaults to ONE step, so the planner and query agent threw `NoOutputGeneratedError` as soon as the model called a tool (reproduced with a mock model). Fixed with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(n)`. Also `financialExposure: z.number().default(0)` broke strict JSON-schema output (missing from `required`); now required.
- **Web env**: `next.config.mjs` loads the repo-root `.env`/`.env.local` (Next only reads `apps/web`), matching SUBMISSION.md.
- **New**: `npm run setup:azure` (Azure CLI script), `npm run verify:llm` (live check: each role responds; planner/reviewer do tool call + structured output), `npm run agent:test`.

## Still open (not done)

- **Reviewer/router/executor roles are never called.** README, SUBMISSION, PATH-ONE describe an independent review step that does not exist in code.
- **PATH-ONE overclaims kernel logic:** kernel never reads `approvalRequirementIds` or policy `priority`, and does not handle `contradicts` evidence (only /observe mentions high-confidence evidence). Conflict detection is "two applicable policies share a scope".
- **PATH-TWO** says the UI opens on a Company State panel (none exists), says "~70 seed docs" (actual: 52), and "one weekend" conflicts with the rest of the narrative. — **Fixed 2026-09-21 (later still), see below.**
- **Kernel tier quirk:** risk between auto-max and review threshold (default: 3) returns `recommendation: execute-autonomously` with `requiresApproval: true`; the UI keys off `recommendation` for the label.
- **Demo variance:** Execute's simulated outcome is seeded by decision id. Ids are now time-based (append-only audit trail), so the -20% branch is ~70%, not guaranteed on every run; the demo script's backup scene covers it.
- `/observe` reads the latest metric of any decision. Runtime doc/metric ids containing a dot (`decision.rollback.*`, `metric.*`) may behave differently from plain ids in Sanity (check before making the dataset public).
- ARCHITECTURE.md says nine types (ten with `metric`). — **Fixed 2026-09-21 (later still).** `QUICKSILVER_RISK_PROHIBITED` is never read.
- No LICENSE, no `.git`, repo URL and demo video are placeholders; SUBMISSION.md has a dangling "Token" line. Rotate any test token before making anything public. `.gitignore` covers `.env`, `.env.local`, `*.log`. — **LICENSE + `.git` + public repo done 2026-09-21 (later still); repo URL placeholders fixed same pass; demo video still outstanding.**
- Decide the public-dataset step (`sanity dataset visibility set production public`) deliberately: it exposes the whole dataset. — **Still outstanding.**
- **`knowledge_base_read` is referenced in the planner/query prompts but was never wired up.** Both `PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and the planner/query task prompts tell the model it has a `knowledge_base_read` tool, but the agent only ever connects to one (GROQ-mode) Context MCP client — one endpoint serves one mode, so that tool has never actually been available. The seed `evidence.ts` data (reports/analyses/memos with explicit `contradictsEvidenceIds`, e.g. engineering analysis vs. historical incident report, VP Engineering procedure vs. VP Operations memo) is a strong, low-effort fit for a second KB-mode endpoint: semantic retrieval with citations over exactly the prose content the "killer moment" policy-conflict demo depends on. Not yet built — needs (1) a Knowledge Base + second KB-mode endpoint in the Context dashboard, (2) `mcp.ts`/`planner.ts`/`query.ts` extended to hold two MCP clients and merge their tool sets. Decide before submission whether this is in scope. — **Built and verified live 2026-09-21 (later still), see below.**

## 2026-09-21 (later) — live credentials verified end-to-end

Both previously-"needs live credentials" items are now confirmed working against real services, and three real bugs were found and fixed along the way (all committed to the repo).

**Azure LLM — verified.** `npm run verify:llm` passes fully: all 4 roles (`qs-planner`, `qs-reviewer`, `qs-router`, `qs-executor`) respond, and planner+reviewer pass the tool-call + structured-output (`PlanOutputSchema`) test. Resource created via Azure AI Foundry Classic (the CLI path was abandoned — Full Sail University's tenant enforces Conditional Access/MFA on ARM management-plane calls with no clean non-interactive workaround found). Quota on this subscription only supports `gpt-5-mini` / `gpt-4.1-mini` in East US; every other candidate model (`gpt-5`, `gpt-5-pro`, `o3`, `o3-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-5-nano`) had zero quota across all deployment types/regions, and `gpt-4o`/`model-router` had quota only in a different region requiring a second resource (declined to avoid config fragmentation).

**Sanity Context MCP — verified.** `npm run verify:mcp` passes fully against the real org/dataset: connects, discovers 4 tools (`initial_context`, `groq_query`, `schema_explorer`, `array_field_reader` — no `knowledge_base_read`, since this is a dataset/GROQ-mode endpoint only), fetches the schema overview, and runs real GROQ queries against live data (`count(*[_type=="capability"])` → 10; a 3-entity query returns real docs like `entity-amara-okafor`, `entity-apex-hydraulics`). Org is `ou5ydq271` ("Nuera Ag Tech", created 2026-09-20, admin `nuera.agtech@gmail.com`) — confirmed legitimate after an earlier false alarm (a stale browser login briefly showed 0 orgs for that account). Endpoint `quicksilver-agent` (Dataset/GROQ mode, project `d280bqjc`, dataset `production`, no GROQ filter). Token `SANITY_CONTEXT_TOKEN` is org-scoped with the `Context Viewer` grant.

**Bugs found and fixed while getting there:**
1. **`apps/studio/sanity.cli.ts` had no project identifier and no repo-root env loading.** The Sanity CLI only auto-loads `.env` from the current directory (`apps/studio`), but this repo's one real `.env` lives at the workspace root. `scripts/deploy-schema.ts` already worked around this with its own manual walk-up loader; `sanity.cli.ts` had nothing, so any direct `sanity deploy`/`sanity schema deploy` invocation failed with "does not contain a project identifier." Tried porting the same walk-up-and-load-into-`process.env` pattern into `sanity.cli.ts` — confirmed by live testing that Sanity's own CLI config loader does not reliably run that side effect before reading `api.projectId` (unlike `tsx`-executed scripts). Fixed by hardcoding the known, non-secret `projectId`/`dataset` values directly (env vars still override), which is the conventional way real-world `sanity.cli.ts` files are written anyway.
2. **`npm run schema:deploy` (the experimental `sanity schema deploy` / schema-store command) has a broken or undocumented non-interactive auth path.** Repeatedly failed with `401 Unauthorized - Session not found` — reproduced across a revoked-then-recreated org token, a completely fresh token from a confirmed Administrator account, and a fresh interactive `sanity logout && sanity login`. The Sanity docs mark this specific command "experimental and subject to change" and don't document its auth behavior, unlike plain `sanity deploy`. **Fix: use `sanity deploy` instead** (from `apps/studio`) — it deploys the schema as part of deploying the actual Studio app, is stable/documented, worked immediately with the same login session that `schema deploy` rejected, and is literally what the Context MCP's own error message asks for ("Only datasets with deployed Studio applications are supported. Please deploy a Studio"). Studio is now live at **https://qkslvr.sanity.studio/**. Recommend retiring or fixing `scripts/deploy-schema.ts` before submission so `npm run schema:deploy` isn't left as a documented step that doesn't reliably work.
3. **`packages/agent/src/verify-mcp.ts`'s sample GROQ query was invalid for this endpoint.** The combined object-literal query (`{ capabilities: count(...), entities: *[...]{...} }`) isn't accepted by this GROQ engine — reported a syntax error pointing at the very end of the query, as if `count(`'s parens were never closed. Fixed by splitting into two plain single-expression queries (`count(*[_type=="capability"])` and a separate entity projection), which is also just simpler. Added `isError` checking so a future failure here is visible instead of silently printing an error payload under a "✓ MCP integration verified" banner.

**Still not done:** the KB-mode / `knowledge_base_read` gap noted above, and everything else in "Still open" — reviewer/router/executor roles, doc overclaims, LICENSE/`.git`, etc. Next: `npm run dev:web` and walk a real objective through the full pipeline (plan → kernel → decision doc → approval).

## 2026-09-21 (final) — full app verified end-to-end live, one more real bug found and fixed

Ran the actual app (`npm run dev:web`) and drove the full loop through the browser: submitted the pre-filled CEO Intent ("Reduce production downtime by 20% over the next 30 days without increasing OPEX.") and walked one decision all the way through **plan → kernel authorize → persisted decision → approve → execute (simulated) → observe metric**.

**Bug found: the live write path (`/api/plan`, `/decisions/[id]/{action,execute,observe,rollback}`) was failing with `500 Unauthorized - Session not found`.** Root cause: all 5 of these routes build their Sanity client with `token: process.env.SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN`, distinct from `SANITY_CONTEXT_TOKEN` (read-only, used only by the Context MCP) — and this token was stale/invalid; it had never actually been fixed, only worked around at the CLI level via interactive `sanity login`, which doesn't touch `.env` at all. The code comment on `getSanityClient()` in `apps/web/app/api/plan/route.ts` already specified the fix: "needs an Editor-scoped token to persist decisions." Created a new org token ("Quicksilver App Writer") scoped to **Project access → Sanity Challenge → Editor** only, with no organization-wide permissions — the token dashboard's project-access role picker fought browser automation for a while (a stray keystroke briefly over-granted several org-wide checkboxes including Manage Access; caught and fully reverted before saving, nothing was ever persisted with the bad grants). User copied the token value directly into `.env` as `SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN` (never seen or handled in chat).

**Result — the full pipeline works end-to-end against live services:**
- Planner queried the real company model via the Context MCP and grounded its plan in actual doc IDs: capabilities (`cap-process-simulation`, `cap-machine-diagnostics`, etc.), entities (`entity-jin-tanaka`, `entity-tom-bradley`, `entity-ravi-patel`), policies (`policy-ops-17`, `policy-emergency-4`, `policy-maint-12`, `policy-budget-3`, `policy-quality-8`), and evidence (`evidence-eng-analysis-c2`, `evidence-maint-847`, `evidence-historical-17`, `evidence-vendor-bulletin-jun25`).
- Kernel authorization worked correctly on all 5 candidate actions: two flagged a real **policy conflict** (Emergency Policy 4 vs. Operations Policy 17 both scoped to `production.parameter_changes`) and were routed to `request-approval`; one (tool replenishment) was **auto-rejected** by the kernel for having no supporting evidence, exactly as designed; the rest awaited approval with correct risk/exposure/reversibility fields.
- Approving the lowest-risk decision (Process Simulation, risk 1/5, $0 exposure, reversible) walked it through **Execute (Simulated) → Observe Metric**, producing a real closed-loop observation: weekly downtime baseline 32 hrs/week → current 25.85 hrs/week (**-19.2%**), plus a surfaced caution referencing the contradicting high-confidence evidence.

This confirms the core thesis end-to-end on live infrastructure: Sanity Context MCP (read) + Azure LLM (reason) + Sanity HTTP API (write) + kernel (authorize) all working together as one loop, not just in isolated component tests.

**Still not done** (unchanged from above): KB-mode / `knowledge_base_read` wiring, reviewer/router/executor roles never invoked, various doc overclaims (PATH-ONE, PATH-TWO, ARCHITECTURE.md), no LICENSE/`.git`, kernel tier quirk, demo variance, dotted decision/metric IDs, unused `QUICKSILVER_RISK_PROHIBITED`, placeholder repo URL/demo video, dangling "Token" line in SUBMISSION.md, and the public-dataset decision.

## 2026-09-21 (contest-requirements audit) — official rules vs. current state, prioritized plan

Pulled the actual official rules (DEV.to challenge post + linked rules page `dev.to/challenges/sanity-2026-09-16`), not just the README's paraphrase, and compared them against everything actually built and drafted so far. Deadline: **October 4, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT** (13 days out from this audit). Winners announced Oct 22. # Quicksilver pre-submission audit (2026-09-21)

## Status: the five blockers are fixed in the repo (same day)

Verified in a scratch copy with the new dependency set: kernel tests 14/14, agent model tests 10/10, an end-to-end route flow (plan -> persist -> approve -> execute -> observe) against the real seed data (52 docs) in an in-memory Sanity, `tsc --noEmit` clean for kernel/agent/web, and `next build` succeeds. The new threshold tests fail against the old `approval.ts`, as they should.

NOT verified (needs live credentials): Azure deployments (strict JSON-schema output, Responses API on your chosen models), the live Sanity Context MCP, and `npm run setup:azure` against the real Azure CLI (tested against a fake `az`, on Linux only).

### What changed
- **Kernel** (`approval.ts`): risk thresholds read via `readRiskThreshold()` with explicit defaults (auto max 2, review 3); unset/empty/garbage/out-of-range env falls back instead of NaN. `AuthorizeResult` now carries `policyChecks`. `types.ts` accepts `null` for `expirationDate`/`reportsToId` (what Sanity returns). 5 new tests.
- **/api/plan**: GROQ fixed (`arr[]._ref`, aliased); persists one `decision` doc per candidate in a single transaction (`decision-plan-<run>-<i>`, status `awaiting-approval`, or `rejected` on a kernel hard block) and returns `decisionDocId`; response now matches its documented shape (`capability.riskLevel`); uses `isLlmConfigured()` instead of requiring `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **/observe**: `"evidenceIds": evidence[]._ref`.
- **/action** (beyond the five): only `awaiting-approval`/`proposed` decisions can be acted on (409 otherwise, so a kernel `reject` is final); approval no longer stamps `executedAt`.
- **AI SDK**: whole stack aligned on the v6 line (`ai@6`, `@ai-sdk/azure@3`, `openai@3`, `anthropic@3`, `google@3`, `openai-compatible@2` for Ollama, `mcp@1`). The old mix was `ai@5` + `anthropic@1` + `azure@4` (spec v4), which cannot work together. Azure is the default provider when `AZURE_API_KEY` + `AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME` are set; deployments `qs-planner|reviewer|router|executor`. Lockfile regenerated.
- **Found while fixing** (not in the original list): `generateText` defaults to ONE step, so the planner and query agent threw `NoOutputGeneratedError` as soon as the model called a tool (reproduced with a mock model). Fixed with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(n)`. Also `financialExposure: z.number().default(0)` broke strict JSON-schema output (missing from `required`); now required.
- **Web env**: `next.config.mjs` loads the repo-root `.env`/`.env.local` (Next only reads `apps/web`), matching SUBMISSION.md.
- **New**: `npm run setup:azure` (Azure CLI script), `npm run verify:llm` (live check: each role responds; planner/reviewer do tool call + structured output), `npm run agent:test`.

## Still open (not done)

- **Reviewer/router/executor roles are never called.** README, SUBMISSION, PATH-ONE describe an independent review step that does not exist in code.
- **PATH-ONE overclaims kernel logic:** kernel never reads `approvalRequirementIds` or policy `priority`, and does not handle `contradicts` evidence (only /observe mentions high-confidence evidence). Conflict detection is "two applicable policies share a scope".

- `/observe` reads the latest metric of any decision. Runtime doc/metric ids containing a dot (`decision.rollback.*`, `metric.*`) may behave differently from plain ids in Sanity (check before making the dataset public).
- ARCHITECTURE.md says nine types (ten with `metric`). — **Fixed 2026-09-21 (later still).** `QUICKSILVER_RISK_PROHIBITED` is never read.
- No LICENSE, no `.git`, repo URL and demo video are placeholders; SUBMISSION.md has a dangling "Token" line. Rotate any test token before making anything public. `.gitignore` covers `.env`, `.env.local`, `*.log`. — **LICENSE + `.git` + public repo done 2026-09-21 (later still); repo URL placeholders fixed same pass; demo video still outstanding.**
- Decide the public-dataset step (`sanity dataset visibility set production public`) deliberately: it exposes the whole dataset. — **Still outstanding.**
- **`knowledge_base_read` is referenced in the planner/query prompts but was never wired up.** Both `PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and the planner/query task prompts tell the model it has a `knowledge_base_read` tool, but the agent only ever connects to one (GROQ-mode) Context MCP client — one endpoint serves one mode, so that tool has never actually been available. Not yet built — needs (1) a Knowledge Base + second KB-mode endpoint in the Context dashboard, (2) `mcp.ts`/`planner.ts`/`query.ts` extended to hold two MCP clients and merge their tool sets. **Bugs found and fixed while getting there:**
1. **`apps/studio/sanity.cli.ts` had no project identifier and no repo-root env loading.** The Sanity CLI only auto-loads `.env` from the current directory (`apps/studio`), but this repo's one real `.env` lives at the workspace root. `scripts/deploy-schema.ts` already worked around this with its own manual walk-up loader; `sanity.cli.ts` had nothing, so any direct `sanity deploy`/`sanity schema deploy` invocation failed with "does not contain a project identifier." Tried porting the same walk-up-and-load-into-`process.env` pattern into `sanity.cli.ts` — confirmed by live testing that Sanity's own CLI config loader does not reliably run that side effect before reading `api.projectId` (unlike `tsx`-executed scripts). Fixed by hardcoding the known, non-secret `projectId`/`dataset` values directly (env vars still override), which is the conventional way real-world `sanity.cli.ts` files are written anyway.
2. **`npm run schema:deploy` (the experimental `sanity schema deploy` / schema-store command) has a broken or undocumented non-interactive auth path.** Repeatedly failed with `401 Unauthorized - Session not found` — reproduced across a revoked-then-recreated org token, a completely fresh token from a confirmed Administrator account, and a fresh interactive `sanity logout && sanity login`. The Sanity docs mark this specific command "experimental and subject to change" and don't document its auth behavior, unlike plain `sanity deploy`. **Fix: use `sanity deploy` instead** (from `apps/studio`) — it deploys the schema as part of deploying the actual Studio app, is stable/documented, worked immediately with the same login session that `schema deploy` rejected, and is literally what the Context MCP's own error message asks for ("Only datasets with deployed Studio applications are supported. Please deploy a Studio"). Studio is now live at **https://qkslvr.sanity.studio/**. Recommend retiring or fixing `scripts/deploy-schema.ts` before submission so `npm run schema:deploy` isn't left as a documented step that doesn't reliably work.
3. **`packages/agent/src/verify-mcp.ts`'s sample GROQ query was invalid for this endpoint.** The combined object-literal query (`{ capabilities: count(...), entities: *[...]{...} }`) isn't accepted by this GROQ engine — reported a syntax error pointing at the very end of the query, as if `count(`'s parens were never closed. Fixed by splitting into two plain single-expression queries (`count(*[_type=="capability"])` and a separate entity projection), which is also just simpler. Added `isError` checking so a future failure here is visible instead of silently printing an error payload under a "✓ MCP integration verified" banner.

**Still not done:** the KB-mode / `knowledge_base_read` gap noted above, and everything else in "Still open" — reviewer/router/executor roles, doc overclaims, LICENSE/`.git`, etc. Next: `npm run dev:web` and walk a real objective through the full pipeline (plan → kernel → decision doc → approval).

## 2026-09-21 (final) — full app verified end-to-end live, one more real bug found and fixed

Ran the actual app (`npm run dev:web`) and drove the full loop through the browser: submitted the pre-filled CEO Intent ("Reduce production downtime by 20% over the next 30 days without increasing OPEX.") and walked one decision all the way through **plan → kernel authorize → persisted decision → approve → execute (simulated) → observe metric**.

**Bug found: the live write path (`/api/plan`, `/decisions/[id]/{action,execute,observe,rollback}`) was failing with `500 Unauthorized - Session not found`.** Root cause: all 5 of these routes build their Sanity client with `token: process.env.SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN`, distinct from `SANITY_CONTEXT_TOKEN` (read-only, used only by the Context MCP) — and this token was stale/invalid; it had never actually been fixed, only worked around at the CLI level via interactive `sanity login`, which doesn't touch `.env` at all. The code comment on `getSanityClient()` in `apps/web/app/api/plan/route.ts` already specified the fix: "needs an Editor-scoped token to persist decisions." # Quicksilver pre-submission audit (2026-09-21)

## Status: the five blockers are fixed in the repo (same day)

Verified in a scratch copy with the new dependency set: kernel tests 14/14, agent model tests 10/10, an end-to-end route flow (plan -> persist -> approve -> execute -> observe) against the real seed data (52 docs) in an in-memory Sanity, `tsc --noEmit` clean for kernel/agent/web, and `next build` succeeds. The new threshold tests fail against the old `approval.ts`, as they should.

NOT verified (needs live credentials): Azure deployments (strict JSON-schema output, Responses API on your chosen models), the live Sanity Context MCP, and `npm run setup:azure` against the real Azure CLI (tested against a fake `az`, on Linux only).

### What changed
- **Kernel** (`approval.ts`): risk thresholds read via `readRiskThreshold()` with explicit defaults (auto max 2, review 3); unset/empty/garbage/out-of-range env falls back instead of NaN. `AuthorizeResult` now carries `policyChecks`. `types.ts` accepts `null` for `expirationDate`/`reportsToId` (what Sanity returns). 5 new tests.
- **/api/plan**: GROQ fixed (`arr[]._ref`, aliased); persists one `decision` doc per candidate in a single transaction (`decision-plan-<run>-<i>`, status `awaiting-approval`, or `rejected` on a kernel hard block) and returns `decisionDocId`; response now matches its documented shape (`capability.riskLevel`); uses `isLlmConfigured()` instead of requiring `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **/observe**: `"evidenceIds": evidence[]._ref`.
- **/action** (beyond the five): only `awaiting-approval`/`proposed` decisions can be acted on (409 otherwise, so a kernel `reject` is final); approval no longer stamps `executedAt`.
- **AI SDK**: whole stack aligned on the v6 line (`ai@6`, `@ai-sdk/azure@3`, `openai@3`, `anthropic@3`, `google@3`, `openai-compatible@2` for Ollama, `mcp@1`). The old mix was `ai@5` + `anthropic@1` + `azure@4` (spec v4), which cannot work together. Azure is the default provider when `AZURE_API_KEY` + `AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME` are set; deployments `qs-planner|reviewer|router|executor`. Lockfile regenerated.
- **Found while fixing** (not in the original list): `generateText` defaults to ONE step, so the planner and query agent threw `NoOutputGeneratedError` as soon as the model called a tool (reproduced with a mock model). Fixed with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(n)`. Also `financialExposure: z.number().default(0)` broke strict JSON-schema output (missing from `required`); now required.
- **Web env**: `next.config.mjs` loads the repo-root `.env`/`.env.local` (Next only reads `apps/web`), matching SUBMISSION.md.
- **New**: `npm run setup:azure` (Azure CLI script), `npm run verify:llm` (live check: each role responds; planner/reviewer do tool call + structured output), `npm run agent:test`.

## Still open (not done)

- ~~**Reviewer/router/executor roles are never called.**~~ **Reviewer wired 2026-09-22, see below.** Router/executor roles remain prompted-for but unused (no code path currently needs a second planner-alternative or a literal executor call beyond the simulated-execution route handler).
- **PATH-ONE overclaims kernel logic:** kernel never reads `approvalRequirementIds` or policy `priority`, and does not handle `contradicts` evidence (only /observe mentions high-confidence evidence). Conflict detection is "two applicable policies share a scope".
- **PATH-TWO** says the UI opens on a Company State panel (none exists), says "~70 seed docs" (actual: 52), and "one weekend" conflicts with the rest of the narrative. — **Fixed 2026-09-21 (later still), see below.**
- **Kernel tier quirk:** risk between auto-max and review threshold (default: 3) returns `recommendation: execute-autonomously` with `requiresApproval: true`; the UI keys off `recommendation` for the label.
- **Demo variance:** Execute's simulated outcome is seeded by decision id. Ids are now time-based (append-only audit trail), so the -20% branch is ~70%, not guaranteed on every run; the demo script's backup scene covers it.
- `/observe` reads the latest metric of any decision. Runtime doc/metric ids containing a dot (`decision.rollback.*`, `metric.*`) may behave differently from plain ids in Sanity (check before making the dataset public).
- ARCHITECTURE.md says nine types (ten with `metric`). — **Fixed 2026-09-21 (later still).** `QUICKSILVER_RISK_PROHIBITED` is never read.
- No LICENSE, no `.git`, repo URL and demo video are placeholders; SUBMISSION.md has a dangling "Token" line. Rotate any test token before making anything public. `.gitignore` covers `.env`, `.env.local`, `*.log`. — **LICENSE + `.git` + public repo done 2026-09-21 (later still); repo URL placeholders fixed same pass; demo video still outstanding.**
- Decide the public-dataset step (`sanity dataset visibility set production public`) deliberately: it exposes the whole dataset. — **Still outstanding.**
- **`knowledge_base_read` is referenced in the planner/query prompts but was never wired up.** Both `PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and the planner/query task prompts tell the model it has a `knowledge_base_read` tool, but the agent only ever connects to one (GROQ-mode) Context MCP client — one endpoint serves one mode, so that tool has never actually been available. The seed `evidence.ts` data (reports/analyses/memos with explicit `contradictsEvidenceIds`, e.g. engineering analysis vs. historical incident report, VP Engineering procedure vs. VP Operations memo) is a strong, low-effort fit for a second KB-mode endpoint: semantic retrieval with citations over exactly the prose content the "killer moment" policy-conflict demo depends on. Not yet built — needs (1) a Knowledge Base + second KB-mode endpoint in the Context dashboard, (2) `mcp.ts`/`planner.ts`/`query.ts` extended to hold two MCP clients and merge their tool sets. Decide before submission whether this is in scope. — **Built and verified live 2026-09-21 (later still), see below.**

## 2026-09-21 (later) — live credentials verified end-to-end

Both previously-"needs live credentials" items are now confirmed working against real services, and three real bugs were found and fixed along the way (all committed to the repo).

**Azure LLM — verified.** `npm run verify:llm` passes fully: all 4 roles (`qs-planner`, `qs-reviewer`, `qs-router`, `qs-executor`) respond, and planner+reviewer pass the tool-call + structured-output (`PlanOutputSchema`) test. Resource created via Azure AI Foundry Classic (the CLI path was abandoned — Full Sail University's tenant enforces Conditional Access/MFA on ARM management-plane calls with no clean non-interactive workaround found). Quota on this subscription only supports `gpt-5-mini` / `gpt-4.1-mini` in East US; every other candidate model (`gpt-5`, `gpt-5-pro`, `o3`, `o3-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-5-nano`) had zero quota across all deployment types/regions, and `gpt-4o`/`model-router` had quota only in a different region requiring a second resource (declined to avoid config fragmentation).

**Sanity Context MCP — verified.** `npm run verify:mcp` passes fully against the real org/dataset: connects, discovers 4 tools (`initial_context`, `groq_query`, `schema_explorer`, `array_field_reader` — no `knowledge_base_read`, since this is a dataset/GROQ-mode endpoint only), fetches the schema overview, and runs real GROQ queries against live data (`count(*[_type=="capability"])` → 10; a 3-entity query returns real docs like `entity-amara-okafor`, `entity-apex-hydraulics`). Org is `ou5ydq271` ("Nuera Ag Tech", created 2026-09-20, admin `nuera.agtech@gmail.com`) — confirmed legitimate after an earlier false alarm (a stale browser login briefly showed 0 orgs for that account). Endpoint `quicksilver-agent` (Dataset/GROQ mode, project `d280bqjc`, dataset `production`, no GROQ filter). Token `SANITY_CONTEXT_TOKEN` is org-scoped with the `Context Viewer` grant.

**Bugs found and fixed while getting there:**
1. **`apps/studio/sanity.cli.ts` had no project identifier and no repo-root env loading.** The Sanity CLI only auto-loads `.env` from the current directory (`apps/studio`), but this repo's one real `.env` lives at the workspace root. `scripts/deploy-schema.ts` already worked around this with its own manual walk-up loader; `sanity.cli.ts` had nothing, so any direct `sanity deploy`/`sanity schema deploy` invocation failed with "does not contain a project identifier." Tried porting the same walk-up-and-load-into-`process.env` pattern into `sanity.cli.ts` — confirmed by live testing that Sanity's own CLI config loader does not reliably run that side effect before reading `api.projectId` (unlike `tsx`-executed scripts). Fixed by hardcoding the known, non-secret `projectId`/`dataset` values directly (env vars still override), which is the conventional way real-world `sanity.cli.ts` files are written anyway.
2. **`npm run schema:deploy` (the experimental `sanity schema deploy` / schema-store command) has a broken or undocumented non-interactive auth path.** Repeatedly failed with `401 Unauthorized - Session not found` — reproduced across a revoked-then-recreated org token, a completely fresh token from a confirmed Administrator account, and a fresh interactive `sanity logout && sanity login`. The Sanity docs mark this specific command "experimental and subject to change" and don't document its auth behavior, unlike plain `sanity deploy`. **Fix: use `sanity deploy` instead** (from `apps/studio`) — it deploys the schema as part of deploying the actual Studio app, is stable/documented, worked immediately with the same login session that `schema deploy` rejected, and is literally what the Context MCP's own error message asks for ("Only datasets with deployed Studio applications are supported. Please deploy a Studio"). Studio is now live at **https://qkslvr.sanity.studio/**. Recommend retiring or fixing `scripts/deploy-schema.ts` before submission so `npm run schema:deploy` isn't left as a documented step that doesn't reliably work.
3. **`packages/agent/src/verify-mcp.ts`'s sample GROQ query was invalid for this endpoint.** The combined object-literal query (`{ capabilities: count(...), entities: *[...]{...} }`) isn't accepted by this GROQ engine — reported a syntax error pointing at the very end of the query, as if `count(`'s parens were never closed. Fixed by splitting into two plain single-expression queries (`count(*[_type=="capability"])` and a separate entity projection), which is also just simpler. Added `isError` checking so a future failure here is visible instead of silently printing an error payload under a "✓ MCP integration verified" banner.

**Still not done:** the KB-mode / `knowledge_base_read` gap noted above, and everything else in "Still open" — reviewer/router/executor roles, doc overclaims, LICENSE/`.git`, etc. Next: `npm run dev:web` and walk a real objective through the full pipeline (plan → kernel → decision doc → approval).

## 2026-09-21 (final) — full app verified end-to-end live, one more real bug found and fixed

Ran the actual app (`npm run dev:web`) and drove the full loop through the browser: submitted the pre-filled CEO Intent ("Reduce production downtime by 20% over the next 30 days without increasing OPEX.") and walked one decision all the way through **plan → kernel authorize → persisted decision → approve → execute (simulated) → observe metric**.

**Bug found: the live write path (`/api/plan`, `/decisions/[id]/{action,execute,observe,rollback}`) was failing with `500 Unauthorized - Session not found`.** Root cause: all 5 of these routes build their Sanity client with `token: process.env.SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN`, distinct from `SANITY_CONTEXT_TOKEN` (read-only, used only by the Context MCP) — and this token was stale/invalid; it had never actually been fixed, only worked around at the CLI level via interactive `sanity login`, which doesn't touch `.env` at all. The code comment on `getSanityClient()` in `apps/web/app/api/plan/route.ts` already specified the fix: "needs an Editor-scoped token to persist decisions." Created a new org token ("Quicksilver App Writer") scoped to **Project access → Sanity Challenge → Editor** only, with no organization-wide permissions — the token dashboard's project-access role picker fought browser automation for a while (a stray keystroke briefly over-granted several org-wide checkboxes including Manage Access; caught and fully reverted before saving, nothing was ever persisted with the bad grants). User copied the token value directly into `.env` as `SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN` (never seen or handled in chat).

**Result — the full pipeline works end-to-end against live services:**
- Planner queried the real company model via the Context MCP and grounded its plan in actual doc IDs: capabilities (`cap-process-simulation`, `cap-machine-diagnostics`, etc.), entities (`entity-jin-tanaka`, `entity-tom-bradley`, `entity-ravi-patel`), policies (`policy-ops-17`, `policy-emergency-4`, `policy-maint-12`, `policy-budget-3`, `policy-quality-8`), and evidence (`evidence-eng-analysis-c2`, `evidence-maint-847`, `evidence-historical-17`, `evidence-vendor-bulletin-jun25`).
- Kernel authorization worked correctly on all 5 candidate actions: two flagged a real **policy conflict** (Emergency Policy 4 vs. Operations Policy 17 both scoped to `production.parameter_changes`) and were routed to `request-approval`; one (tool replenishment) was **auto-rejected** by the kernel for having no supporting evidence, exactly as designed; the rest awaited approval with correct risk/exposure/reversibility fields.
- Approving the lowest-risk decision (Process Simulation, risk 1/5, $0 exposure, reversible) walked it through **Execute (Simulated) → Observe Metric**, producing a real closed-loop observation: weekly downtime baseline 32 hrs/week → current 25.85 hrs/week (**-19.2%**), plus a surfaced caution referencing the contradicting high-confidence evidence.

This confirms the core thesis end-to-end on live infrastructure: Sanity Context MCP (read) + Azure LLM (reason) + Sanity HTTP API (write) + kernel (authorize) all working together as one loop, not just in isolated component tests.

- **`apps/web/app/api/plan/route.ts`**: after the kernel's `authorize()` call for each candidate action (only when actor+capability resolved), now also calls `reviewProposedAction()` with the same actor/capability/policies/evidence, mapped to the shapes it expects. `buildDecisionDoc()` takes the review result and includes it as `reviewerNotes` on the persisted `decision` document (`undefined` when there was no review, so no dangling field on unresolved candidates). The API response's `decisions[]` array now includes `review: ReviewResult | null` alongside the existing `decision` field. Top-of-file doc comment renumbered (now 7 steps) and states plainly that the kernel is "the only authoritative step" and the reviewer is "ADVISORY ONLY, never changes the kernel's outcome."
- **`apps/web/app/page.tsx`**: `DecisionResponse` type gained a `review: ReviewResult | null` field. `DecisionCard` renders a new panel (dashed border, distinct from the kernel's own policy-conflict/concern/blocking-reason blocks) titled "Independent review (advisory, not a gate)", placed after the kernel's `blockingReasons` block and before the lifecycle action buttons. It shows "No concerns raised." when all four review arrays are empty, or renders each non-empty array with its own icon/color (⚠ policy conflicts in red, `?` missing evidence and `!` risk concerns in yellow, `→` suggestions in the accent color) — visually distinct from the kernel's own red/yellow markers so a judge can tell at a glance which system (deterministic kernel vs. advisory LLM reviewer) is saying what.

All five files pushed to the user's Windows machine via `device_commit_files` and verified byte-for-byte via an immediate `device_stage_files` read-back (per the mount-propagation-race lesson from the KB-mode work) — all landed correctly on the first attempt this time.

**Checked the docs for a stale "not wired" honesty caveat that would now need removing:** grepped `SUBMISSION.md`, `README.md`, `docs/PATH-ONE.md`, `docs/PATH-TWO.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` for reviewer-related text. None of them actually contained an explicit "not yet called" disclaimer — the honesty gap flagged in the contest-requirements audit above was that these docs described the reviewer as if it were already live (which was the overclaim), not that they contained a caveat needing removal. Now that the code matches the docs, no further doc edits were needed for this item.

**Not yet done (still needs the user, since it requires their terminal or a live browser session against their Sanity org):**
- Run `sanity deploy` from `apps/studio` so the new `reviewerNotes` schema field actually takes effect.
- Re-run the app (`npm run dev:web`) and drive one objective through `/api/plan` live to confirm the reviewer panel renders with real content (not just the neutral fallback).
- Update `SUBMISSION.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`/`README.md`/`docs/PATH-ONE.md` to state the reviewer is now demonstrably wired in with a live example, once that live confirmation exists (optional — the docs didn't overclaim in a way that strictly requires this, but a real example strengthens Path One's "technical implementation" case).

**What's left overall, per the user's expanded request (tasks #18–#21):**
1. Make the Sanity dataset public for judges (`sanity dataset visibility set production public`) — one command, deliberate decision, not yet run. (Task #18 — also need to check whether the Sanity Manage UI exposes this as a toggle, as an alternative to handing the user a CLI command, since this session has no shell access to the user's machine.)
2. Add a one-line "no login required" testing-access note to `docs/PATH-ONE.md` and `docs/PATH-TWO.md`. (Task #19)
3. Research whether DEV's Agent Sessions Uploader (`dev.to/agent_sessions/new`) can actually take this session's transcript in a usable format. (Task #20)
4. Nice-to-have cleanup: kernel tier quirk (risk between auto-max and review threshold labeled `execute-autonomously` with `requiresApproval: true`), dotted decision/metric IDs, unused `QUICKSILVER_RISK_PROHIBITED` env var, dangling "Token" line in `SUBMISSION.md`, one more token rotation right before going public. (Task #21)
5. Beyond the formal task list: record the demo video per `docs/DEMO-SCRIPT.md`, consider a live Vercel deployment, format and publish both DEV.to posts with `#sanitychallenge`, and — after everything else — consider a lightweight Sanity Workflow around the decision lifecycle as Path Two's optional bonus feature.

entries.description:
Use this tool to retrieve a task by its ID from the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- When you need the full description and context before starting work on a task
- To understand task dependencies (what it blocks, what blocks it)
- After being assigned a task, to get complete requirements

## Output

Returns full task details:
- **subject**: Task title
- **description**: Detailed requirements and context
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **blocks**: Tasks waiting on this one to complete
- **blockedBy**: Tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Tips

- After fetching a task, verify its blockedBy list is empty before beginning work.
- Use TaskList to see all tasks in summary form.

1	# Path One post — *Quicksilver: An Autonomous Company Operating System*
2	
3	> Path: **Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content**
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Headline
8	
9	**A chatbot reads your documents. Quicksilver reasons over your company.**
10	
11	## Tagline for the cover image
12	
13	`Structured organizational knowledge → agent reasoning → deterministic authority → recorded decision → state update`
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Body
18	
19	Most AI business tools answer questions about your company by searching
20	documents. They find mentions. They confabulate when nothing matches.
21	**Quicksilver is different**: it asks the agent to query a *structured model*
22	of the company — entities, capabilities, policies, evidence, objectives,
23	workflows — and then runs the proposed action through a deterministic
24	authorization kernel before any state changes.
25	
26	The shape of the company comes from Sanity. Ten document types carry it:
27	`organization`, `department`, `entity` (one abstraction for humans,
28	agents, robots, systems, and contractors — same shape, same reasoning),
29	`capability`, `policy`, `objective`, `workflow`, `evidence`, `decision`,
30	`metric`. The schema is in the repo at `apps/studio/schemas/`.
31	
32	The agent reads through Sanity Context MCP — two separate endpoints,
33	since one endpoint serves one mode. The GROQ-mode endpoint exposes
34	`groq_query`, `schema_explorer`, and `array_field_reader` over the live
35	dataset. A second, KB-mode endpoint serves a real Sanity Knowledge Base
36	built from the `evidence` and `policy` documents (with `contradicts[]`
37	unfolded so the target claim's text and confidence are inlined, not
38	just linked) via `knowledge_base_read`. Sanity's own build pipeline
39	grouped that content into cited entries and flagged the central
40	parameter-drift-vs-mechanical-failure conflict as a pending contradiction
41	for review — that detection is a platform feature, not something
42	Quicksilver had to build. The agent's tool set merges both endpoints
43	(`packages/agent/src/mcp.ts`), and `npm run verify:mcp` exercises both
44	live. No keyword search. No fabricated IDs. Every fact the agent cites
45	is a real Sanity document.
46	
47	The kernel is plain TypeScript. No LLM inside it. The LLM proposes a
48	candidate action; the kernel decides whether the actor has the
49	capability, which policies apply, how the risk stacks up, and whether
50	the action is allowed to execute autonomously, requires human approval,
51	or is hard-blocked. Hard blocks (no capability granted, no evidence
52	available) reject. Soft concerns (policy conflicts, low evidence
53	confidence) escalate to approval. Risk above the org-defined threshold
54	always escalates.
55	
56	Models are role-based. The planner is `gpt-5.6-sol` (or
57	`gemini-3.8-flash` after a bake-off — Google's positioning of 3.8 Flash
58	as "engineered for autonomous agents and complex enterprise workflows"
59	makes it a serious candidate). The reviewer is `claude-sonnet-5`, which
60	flags concerns independently. Neither reviewer nor planner is allowed
61	to authorize. The kernel is authoritative.
62	
63	## What the demo proves
64	
65	Drop in the seed objective: *"Reduce production downtime by 20% over the
66	next 30 days without increasing OPEX."* The agent decomposes it,
67	identifies the relevant policies (Operations Policy 17 and Emergency
68	Policy 4, both in scope `production.parameter_changes`), and proposes
69	adjusting a CNC controller parameter by 5%. The kernel's authority
70	check surfaces the conflict (same scope, priority 5 vs. priority 7) and
71	the historical-incident evidence that contradicts the parameter-adjustment
72	hypothesis (confidence 0.92). Risk computes to 4 of 5. Reversibility is
73	partial. The recommendation routes to **human approval**.
74	
75	Approve, execute (simulated), observe a metric moved 32 → 25.6 hours
76	per week, and close the loop. The decision record — what was proposed,
77	what evidence applied, what policies conflicted, what risk level, who
78	approved, what was executed — is persisted as a `decision` doc in
79	Sanity. Auditable. Inspectable.
80	
81	## Why Path One specifically
82	
83	The judging asks: *could this just have been keyword search?* No. A
84	keyword search finds "Engineering approval is required for parameter
85	changes." It does not find:
86	
87	- whether the policy applies (vs. is superseded, expired, or
88	  out-of-scope)
89	- whether the actor has the capability in the company model
90	- whether the actor is on the approval list for this policy
91	- whether a higher-priority policy conflicts
92	- whether evidence contradicts the recommendation at confidence 0.92
93	- what the rollback procedure is
94	- whether the action is reversible
95	- who else is required on the approval chain
96	
97	Quicksilver surfaces all of that *because* the data is structured.
98	Stripping the structure leaves a chatbot. Keeping it leaves an
99	operating system.
100	
101	## Stack
102	
103	| Layer | Choice |
104	|---|---|
105	| Runtime | Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind |
106	| Knowledge substrate | Sanity Studio + Content Lake + Context MCP + Knowledge Bases |
107	| Agent harness | AI SDK 6 + `@ai-sdk/mcp` |
108	| Models | `gpt-5.6-sol`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gemini-3.8-flash` (role-based) |
109	| Authority | Quicksilver Kernel (deterministic TypeScript, no LLM) |
110	| Write path | `@sanity/client` against the Sanity HTTP API |
111	
112	## Repo
113	
114	https://github.com/nuerainc/quicksilver-sanity-challenge — source,
115	schema, kernel tests, smoke test, and README. See `SUBMISSION.md` for
116	the project ID and how to make the dataset public for inspection.
117	
118	## Links
119	
120	- Project URL: https://www.sanity.io/organizations/ou5ydq271/project/d280bqjc
